title: Installing an Under-Sink Carbon Filtration System with Cartridge Indicator (This Old House)

locations.name: Under-sink kitchen cabinet (probable)
locations.basis: Transcript describes the filtration unit intended to sit under the sink; no explicit shooting location is given, so location is inferred from installation context.

summary: This Old House walks through upgrading a retrofit snap-on faucet filtration setup to a dedicated under-sink carbon filtration system with a cartridge-indicator, highlighting the cartridge technology (carbon composite membrane), kit contents, and a step-by-step installation sequence. The presenter covers how the indicator shows cartridge life, how the carbon membrane targets sediment, heavy metals, pesticides, and pharmaceuticals, and then demonstrates removing the old aerator, connecting new supply tubes, choosing push-fit versus compression connections, and finally initializing and flushing the system before testing the water for taste. The workflow emphasizes proper shut-off, secure connections, and a guided diagram to minimize mis-piping, finishing with a tested, cleaner-looking installation under the sink.

sections.title: Transition to permanent under-sink filtration
sections.description: The presenter announces replacing the old snap-on filter with a new filtration unit intended to sit under the sink, and demonstrates the cartridge indicator system that switches from red to blue as the cartridge is used.

sections.title: Filtration cartridge and membrane details
concepts: water flow path through outer/inner tubes
removal of contaminants (heavy metals, pesticides, pharmaceuticals)
sections.description: A cutaway explains the two-tube, two-side flow path inside the carbon membrane cartridge, detailing how water enters, passes through the membrane, and exits, while describing broad contaminant removal capabilities and the potential for roughly a year of cartridge life with reduced replacement frequency.

sections.title: AERATOR and faucet prep
sections.description: The cold side is shut off to relieve pressure, the old faucet aerator is removed, and a new aerator is installed to align the faucet with the new filtration setup.

sections.title: Filtration kit overview and diagram
sections.description: The back of the filtration kit is shown, including tubing connections, adapters, and a diagram that guides correct piping, highlighting the cold-water shut-off symbol and piping flow direction.

sections.title: Disconnecting and replacing supply connections (compression)
sections.description: The presenter demonstrates loosening a compression connection and replacing it with a new supply line, illustrating the basic mechanics of replacing metal/compression fittings for the new unit.

sections.title: Tubing and flow connections (push fittings)
sections.description: A push-fit connection is shown: pressing the tubing in locks it in place, creating a watertight seal. The presenter emphasizes leaving tubes long enough for future service.

sections.title: Finalize installation and initialize
sections.description: The system is set up and re-pressurized before the initialization routine is run: five-minute flush, ten-minute rest, and three more minutes to prepare for testing.

sections.title: Taste test and wrap-up
sections.description: A quick taste test confirms clean water, the presenter praises the improved appearance, and the wrap-up invites viewers to explore more videos and subscribe.

sections.title: Closing remarks
sections.description: The host signs off, noting This Old House has videos on many home improvements and encourages ongoing engagement.
